questions.q: What does a prorate convention determine?
options: The fraction of a full year's depreciation taken in the first (and last) year based on the date placed in service
Which GL account depreciation expense posts to
Whether an asset can be retired
questions.explain: A prorate convention maps the date placed in service to a prorate period, which sets the first-year (and last-year) depreciation fraction.

questions.q: Under a half-year prorate convention, how much depreciation does an asset take in its first year regardless of the exact date placed in service?
options: Zero — half-year conventions defer depreciation to year two
A random percentage set by the user
questions.explain: A half-year convention always assigns exactly half a year of depreciation in year one, regardless of when during the year the asset went into service.

questions.q: What is the difference between a depreciation calendar and a prorate calendar?
options: They are the same thing with two different names
The depreciation calendar defines a book's fiscal years/periods; the prorate calendar maps dates to prorate periods used by conventions
The prorate calendar only exists for tax books
The depreciation calendar is used only for retirements
questions.explain: The depreciation calendar structures how a book calculates and allocates depreciation period by period, while the prorate calendar is the separate structure a prorate convention references.

questions.q: A $10,000-a-year straight-line asset is placed in service August 10 under a mid-month convention, with 5 of 12 months remaining in the fiscal year. What is year-one depreciation?
questions.explain: $10,000 x (5/12) = $4,166.67, since mid-month treats the full month of August as the starting point and five months remain in the year.

questions.q: Does the depreciation calendar have to be identical to the General Ledger's accounting calendar?
options: Yes, Oracle Fusion Assets requires them to be identical
No, they can differ, though many implementations align them to simplify reconciliation
No, and aligning them is never recommended
Depreciation calendars were replaced by prorate calendars in Fusion
questions.explain: The depreciation calendar is a separate structure from the GL calendar; they don't have to match, though keeping them aligned simplifies later reconciliation work.
